_comment: THE SEVEN CATEGORIES THIS KIT DETECTS, AND WHY THE SET IS FIXED RATHER THAN OPEN-ENDED.
A detector that is told 'find anything sensitive' has no way to be wrong in a way that can be
measured -- 'sensitive' means something different to every reader. Naming the seven categories
gives the model a closed schema to fill and gives the eval a closed set of labels to grade
against, the same reason docs-extract's fields.json exists instead of a free-text extraction.
A forker pointing this at a different document set edits this file, not src/prompt.py -- the
prompt is generated FROM this list, the same discipline docs-route's taxonomy.py uses for its
queues. Adding an eighth category (say, PASSPORT_NUMBER) is one entry here plus new labelled
examples; nothing about the pipeline shape changes.

categories.name: NAME
categories.hint: A person's full name, as it appears -- not a title or role alone.

categories.name: SSN
categories.hint: A US Social Security Number, in any format the document writes it: dashed (123-45-6789), undashed (123456789), or labelled inline.

categories.name: PHONE
categories.hint: A phone number, in any format: parenthesised area code, dashed, dotted, or with a country prefix.

categories.name: ADDRESS
categories.hint: A mailing or street address -- street, city, state and/or ZIP together, as one span. Not a city or state named alone in prose.

categories.name: DOB
categories.hint: A date of birth, in any format the document writes it -- numeric, spelled month, or labelled 'DOB'. Not any other date in the document: an appointment date or an issue date is not a DOB.

categories.name: CARD
categories.hint: A payment card number, in any grouping the document writes it -- spaced, dashed, or run together. Not a partial 'ending in ####'.
